Only two messages come from `type_cast_value` itself. Both are `BadParameter` instances, and the code is at `src/click/core.py:2716-2770`.

1. **`Value must be an iterable.`** (line 2734)
   - Raised when `check_iter` gets a value that `_check_iter` rejects with a `TypeError`. The `TypeError` is suppressed with `from None`.
   - `check_iter` runs in three places: the `nargs == -1` converter, the `nargs > 1` converter, and the outer loop when `multiple=True`.
   - So a non-iterable value passed in directly (the comment says this happens only when args are passed manually, not from the command line) fails here. A single-value parameter with `nargs == 1` and `multiple=False` never calls `check_iter`, so it can't raise this.
   - I did not read the body of `_check_iter` (line 2222), so I can't say exactly which values it rejects.

2. **`Takes {nargs} values but 1 was given.`** or **`Takes {nargs} values but {len} were given.`** (lines 2755-2763)
   - Raised only in the `nargs > 1` converter, when the tuple built from the value has a length different from `self.nargs`.
   - `ngettext` picks the singular form only when the length is exactly 1. Any other length, including 0, gets the plural form, e.g. "Takes 2 values but 0 were given."
   - Composite types (`self.type.is_composite`) always take the single-value path, so this length check never runs for them.

Other exceptions can come from `self.type(...)` (lines 2742, 2747, 2765). Those are not raised in `core.py`. Any `BadParameter` or other exception the type raises propagates unchanged; the `Choice` message is one example, but its text lives in `types.py`, which I didn't read.

If `value is None`, the function returns `()` when `multiple` is set or `nargs == -1`, and returns `None` otherwise. No error is raised in that case.

Note: the whole-file `cat` returned an outline with bodies elided, not the full source. I used `ojas read --symbol type_cast_value` to get this function's body. The answer covers only that function. I did not modify any files.
